cash_constraint_contract.summary: Precision Aesthetics Lab is a single‑provider, high‑margin, capacity‑capped aesthetics studio starting from low cash ($15k now, ~$239k at Q1 end) but with very strong modeled profitability and moderate term debt ($120k). The baseline cash path is a straight staircase, compounding cash by ~+90% from the opening seed in Q1 and then by a steady ~+92% over 20 quarters. That path is commercially overstated for this operating model and ignores realistic reinvestment needs (higher owner comp, more realistic rent, incremental staff/support, equipment refresh, and right‑sized marketing). Under a reinvest strategy, this business can and should deploy a meaningful portion of surplus cash into capacity, quality, and sustainability, but not so aggressively that cash becomes tight: the owner still needs resilience and optionality. The contract therefore flattens and introduces real deployment windows relative to the baseline, yielding a more moderate but still steadily rising cash level with distinct periods of heavier reinvestment. Q2–Q4 allow continued buffer building (but below baseline’s pace), Q5–Q8 introduce a clear deployment window with near‑flat/negative quarters to represent step‑ups in compensation, staffing, space quality, and/or equipment, followed by a disciplined rebuild and slower build. By the back half of the horizon, cash growth resumes at a controlled rate, leaving substantial retained cash while reflecting ongoing reinvestment rather than unchecked hoarding.
